news.name: Browns Start 2026 with Rookie-Led Offensive Line Overhaul vs. Jaguars
news.summary: The Cleveland Browns face the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, with rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and rookie right guard Austin Barber starting due to injuries to Teven Jenkins (back) and a questionable Parker Brailsford (thumb). This creates an entirely new starting offensive line from last year's Week 1 group. Fano shared his excitement after practice, saying he and Barber focus on improving daily, while Barber prepared for his NFL debut by staying ready for any role. The Browns also elevated linebacker Nathaniel Watson and cornerback D’Angelo Ross from the practice squad, as the Jaguars deal with their own injury concerns like a questionable LeQuint Allen Jr. and limited Anton Harrison.

news.hook: Odell Beckham Jr. capped up his new platinum hair during practice, teasing fans before revealing it fully. Younger Giants teammates requested the throwback look from his early days.
news.name: Odell Beckham Jr. Revives Blonde Hair for Giants Return
news.summary: Beckham, now 33, dyed his hair blonde after requests from young teammates, calling it a fun 'core memory' tied to his flashy Giants start. The timing builds hype for Sunday's season opener against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium, where he made his iconic 2014 one-handed touchdown catch as a rookie. After signing a one-year deal in June and earning a roster spot, Beckham aims to contribute in a supporting role under new coach John Harbaugh while embracing the nostalgia.

news.hook: Glen Powell, the Austin-born actor and Longhorns fan, stepped up as College GameDay's celebrity picker on the LBJ Library lawn, hyping the massive top-five clash.
news.name: No. 1 Ohio State Faces No. 4 Texas in Austin Tonight
news.summary: ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from the University of Texas campus ahead of the 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, with both undefeated teams coming off blowout Week 1 wins—Ohio State 56-3 over Ball State and Texas 59-7 over Texas State. Fans fired up the rivalry with playful jabs like a sign mocking Ohio State coach Ryan Day for putting ketchup on brisket, a nod to Texas barbecue pride that even GameDay called out as 'No, just no.' Texas coach Steve Sarkisian kept it simple: 'We're talking about a hell of a football game that's gonna get played tonight.' The Longhorns are slight 1.5-point home favorites, airing on ABC.

news.name: Bears Face Panthers in 2026 NFL Season Opener Amid Fan Hype
news.summary: The Chicago Bears visit the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium for a noon CT kickoff on FOX, pitting 2025 division champs against each other—Bears from the NFC North at 11-6, Panthers from the NFC South at 8-9. Quarterbacks Caleb Williams and Bryce Young, linked by a 2023 trade, headline the matchup as fans debate roster edges like offensive lines and skill positions. Chicago enters as a three-point road favorite with expert picks leaning their way, though Carolina hopes a strong home start builds on last year's rally from an 0-2 hole.

news.hook: Nnamdi Madubuike called the past year one of the hardest of his life, yet he never doubted his comeback from neck surgery. Now, he's 'really, really close' but will miss Sunday's opener.
news.name: Ravens' Madubuike Sits Out Season Opener with Neck Injury
news.summary: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, a two-time Pro Bowl player, will sit out the season opener against the Indianapolis Colts as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery from April neck surgery. Coach Jesse Minter described him as ramping up well after missing most of last season, while Madubuike expressed gratitude for the support and determination to return. The Ravens also ruled out linebacker Teddye Buchanan, listed wide receiver Devontez Walker as questionable, and cleared Zay Flowers; the defense will rely on veterans like Calais Campbell to fill the gap.

news.hook: Tua Tagovailoa grabbed his side after a throw in practice, ending his shot at Week 1. Now veteran backup Cooper Rush steps in for the Falcons' opener.
news.name: Falcons Turn to Cooper Rush as Starting QB with Tagovailoa Out
news.summary: The Atlanta Falcons named Cooper Rush their starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after ruling out Tua Tagovailoa with an oblique injury from Thursday practice. Michael Penix Jr., still recovering from a torn ACL, will be the emergency option, with undrafted rookie Jack Strand as backup. Rush, a 32-year-old journeyman with a 9-7 record as a starter, faces a tough Steelers defense that racked up 48 sacks last season amid the team's ongoing quarterback carousel.

news.hook: Josh Allen steps into Houston's stadium where he's never won, facing C.J. Stroud and a defense that's owned him before. It's the NFL's 'unstoppable force meets immovable object' right out of the gate.
news.name: Bills-Texans AFC Clash Kicks Off 2026 Season in Houston
news.summary: The Buffalo Bills open their 2026 campaign on the road against the Houston Texans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET from Reliant Stadium, airing on CBS and Paramount+. Buffalo's offense, boosted by new coach Joe Brady, D.J. Moore, and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, takes on Houston's stout unit led by C.J. Stroud, with Allen holding a 1-4 career record against them and 0-4 at home. While ESPN and CBS analysts pick a narrow Texans win, public betting leans Bills, setting up a high-stakes quarterback duel for two Super Bowl hopefuls.
